notes:
Yesterday's fix for the audit that overran its time limit did not work on the case it was written for.

1.3.53 gave the outbound-link check a deadline: it would take only as many links as the remaining time could afford. That was the right idea and the arithmetic was wrong in the one place it mattered.

The guard asked whether there was budget left. On a site that asks to be crawled slowly, there is not — the crawl has already spent the whole allowance getting through the pages, which is exactly the situation that produced the problem in the first place. With the allowance gone, the guard decided it had nothing to do and let the link check run without a limit, which is what it had always done.

We found it by re-running the same audit that exposed the original problem. It was still going after ten minutes, against a five-minute limit.

An audit whose time is already spent now checks one outbound link rather than sixty. The finding says how many it looked at, as it always has.

**The tests did not catch this and it is worth saying why.** All three of them handed the check a positive amount of time — including the one named for an exhausted budget, which gave it half a second. Half a second is not exhausted. There is now a test that hands it a budget already gone, and it fails against yesterday's release exactly as it should.

Nothing else changes. A crawl that finishes with time in hand still checks every link it selected, and a site that declares no crawl delay is untouched, because there is no time limit to reach when requests cost milliseconds.
